Headline: Borrowing costs climb in Europe and oil tops $105 a barrel as bank says growing price pressures in eurozone will be ‘longer lasting than we had anticipated’
Content: Christine Lagarde, president of the European Central Bank, speaks to the press in Berlin after the rate  decision.Photograph: John MacDougall/AFP/GettyView image in fullscreenChristine Lagarde, president of the European Central Bank, speaks to the press in Berlin after the rate  decision.Photograph: John MacDougall/AFP/GettyEuropean Central BankECB raises interest rates to 2.5% and warns Iran war is fuelling inflationBorrowing costs climb in Europe and oil tops $105 a barrel as bank says growing price pressures in eurozone will be ‘longer lasting than we had anticipated’Business live – latest updatesPhillip InmanandJulia KolleweThu 10 Sep 2026 09.10 EDTLast modified on Thu 10 Sep 2026 11.58 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTheEuropean Central Bankhas raised interest rates to 2.5% and warned that the risk of higher inflation over the next year has risen following renewed fighting in the Middle East.It came as government borrowing costs soared on the back of a jump in oil and gas prices after the latest US andIranattacks on ships in the strait of Hormuz.The interest rate, or yield, on UK government debt rose to a 19-year high on Thursday, while the yield on US and European bonds also climbed in line with oil, which touched $105 (£78) a barrel.Investors had expected the ECB to raise the cost of borrowing across the euro bloc, but were spooked by the hawkish tone of the central bank’s report, which warned of inflationary pressures building in many sectors of the economy.Increasing its main rate from 2.25% to the highest level since March last year, the central bank lifted its forecast for eurozone economic growth in 2026 to 0.9%, up from 0.8% in June. It now expects inflation to average 3% this year.The biggest driving force of rising prices is the cost of energy, which again jumped on Thursday after this week’sincrease in USandIranian attackson ships transiting the Gulf.Brent crude passed $105 a barrel, before slipping back to about $104.5, a 3.3% rise on the day. British gas prices rose to above 203p per therm, the highest since December 2022.Continental European gas prices also increased. The Dutch wholesale gas price – the EU standard – passed €80 per megawatt hour (MWh) for the first time since January 2023. The front-month contract is trading 3.4% higher at €82.56/MWh.This, in turn, increased government borrowing costs in leading economies. The interest rate on benchmark 10-year UK government bonds, also known as gilts, hit 5.36%, the highest since August 2007.Bond yield chartThe rate on Germany’s 30-year government bond rose 2.5 basis points to 5.08%, the highest since December 2003. The 10-year yield hit 3.45%, the highest since April 2011. France’s 10-year government bond yield was the highest since October 2008 at 4.344%, up 1 basis point.Central banks are concerned that high fuel and energy prices will feed into higher transport costs and more expensive heating for commercial and residential properties, which will lead to a broad-based rise in inflation.The ECB president, Christine Lagarde, said: “We believe inflation will be longer lasting than we had anticipated,” adding that food inflation, which had remained low at 1.2%, was likely to increase in response to higher oil and gas prices.She explicitly acknowledged ‌that gas prices could rise owing to further supply disruptions or an unusually cold winter in combination with low storage levels across much of the region.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionInvestors are concerned that UK and EU governments haveunderplayed the risk of running out of gasand the negative effect a subsequent dash for supplies will have on inflation. Recent data shows EU gas stores are only 67% full, well below the five-year average of 84%.UK and continental European gas buyers have delayed filling gas stores in the expectation that the Middle East conflict will be resolved and prices will be lower before winter in the northern hemisphere. As the war drags on, there is the prospect of gas prices rising because of a scramble of buyers looking to replenish stocks before cold weather arrives.Bond markets were also put on alert by the US Treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, who said the US would buy back $6bn worth of government debt – known as US treasuries – in an effort to alleviate a sell-off in the USbond marketthat has put pressure on interest rates.But the size of the packagewas considered inadequate by bond buyersand the yield on 10-year treasuries rose to a three-year high.“Headline inflation is expected to return to around target towards the end of 2027, supported by the effects of higher interest rates,” Lagarde said.Asked about the ECB’s next move, she said: “We have not debated at all any kind of future path. Markets do what they have to do and we do what ​we have to do – which is to provide price stability.”Explore more on these topicsEuropean Central BankMiddle East and north AfricaUS-Israel war on IranStrait of HormuzOilCommoditiesEuropeShareReuse this content

title: The Odyssey and Spider-Man propel record-breaking summer box office worldwide | Film industry | The Guardian
description: The biggest May to September of all time was recorded in US cinemas, with the UK enjoying a 56% rise in audiences, outstripped by an 88% lift in the Middle East and Africa
Author: Catherine Shoard
Headline: The biggest May to September of all time was recorded in US cinemas, with the UK enjoying a 56% rise in audiences, outstripped by an 88% lift in the Middle East and Africa
Content: Hollywood’s Chinese theatre during opening weekend  of The Odyssey in July.Photograph: AaronP/Bauer-Griffin/GC ImagesView image in fullscreenHollywood’s Chinese theatre during opening weekend  of The Odyssey in July.Photograph: AaronP/Bauer-Griffin/GC ImagesFilm industryThe Odyssey and Spider-Man propel record-breaking summer box office worldwideThe biggest May to September of all time was recorded in US cinemas, with the UK enjoying a 56% rise in audiences, outstripped by an 88% lift in the Middle East and AfricaCatherine ShoardThu 10 Sep 2026 09.57 EDTLast modified on Thu 10 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAs well as celebrating their wedding, the actors Tom Holland and Zendaya have something else to toast: their two summer blockbusters –The Odysseyand Spider-Man: Brand New Day – have officially made box office history.The films were credited as the driving force behind the US’s biggest summer season of all time, taking $4.761bn (£3.51bn) from 1 May-7 September, beating 2013’s $4.756bn.Spider-Man is currently on $2.4bn worldwide and likely to climb higher, while The Odyssey has made $1.6bn. Other key titles driving sales include Toy Story 5, Michael and The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, all of which have grossed over $1bn.The breadth of the success of Destin Daniel Cretton’s Spider-Man: Brand New Day was a particular surprise. The film is the best-performing of the year so far and the third highest-grossing film of all time. Its opening weekend was the second-best of all time behind Avengers: Endgame (2019) and it is also the second-fastest film to gross $1bn, doing so in six days.Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, meanwhile, is the highest-grossing “original” movie of the year, despite its adaptation from Homer’s epic poem. Low-budget original horror movies Backrooms ($394m) and Obsession ($513m) have also helped re-energise the box office.Sequels and spinoffs accounted for many of the underperformers, including Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu ($345.4m) , Supergirl ($126.4m) and Minions & Monsters ($518.1m – around half of 2022’s Minions: The Rise of Gru).Meanwhile, August cinema admissions in the UK rose 56% year-on-year to over 17m, according to the UK Cinema Association, signalling the biggest August since 2018 and the second-best performing month since July 2023, when Barbie and Oppenheimer opened together.Such an uptick is dwarfed by the picture in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, which saw an 88% year-on-year lift, according to Gower Street and the International Union of Cinemas. France’s 19.9m August admissions was the best number recorded during that month since records began 46 years ago, and marked a 50% increase from 2025.Italian cinemas recorded their best-ever June-August period, with 20.8m admissions and a take of €162.3m, as well as their best ever August. Spain saw a 71% year-on-year increase, while the Netherlands recorded a 77% lift.Explore more on these topicsFilm industryThe OdysseySpider-Man: Brand New ⁠DaynewsShareReuse this content

title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Nicolas Jackson is ready to impress, Spurs are scrambled and the 199th Manchester derby takes place at Old Trafford
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Nicolas Jackson is ready to impress, Spurs are scrambled and the 199th Manchester derby takes place at Old Trafford
Content: Brentford's Vitaly Janelt, Hull City's Oli McBurnie, Aston Villa's Nicolas Jackson.Composite: Getty, ShutterstockView image in fullscreenBrentford's Vitaly Janelt, Hull City's Oli McBurnie, Aston Villa's Nicolas Jackson.Composite: Getty, ShutterstockTen things to look out for this weekendPremier LeaguePremier League: 10 things to look out for this weekendNicolas Jackson is ready to impress, Spurs are scrambled and the 199th Manchester derby takes place at Old TraffordPremier League top scorers 2026-27: who is leading race for the golden boot?Guardian sportThu 10 Sep 2026 19.01 EDTLast modified on Thu 10 Sep 2026 19.29 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google1Ton up for hard-working McBurnieWith 10 top-flight goal contributions between them across three games already this season, the Chelsea trio of Morgan Rogers, João Pedro and Cole Palmer are the early pace-setters for the Premier League’s most prolific, fluid and high octane attacking unit. But on the occasion of his 100thPremier Leagueappearance, a scruffier and more ungainly unit will be hoping to steal their thunder, as high-flying Hull try to register a top-flight win against Chelsea for the very first time. Yet to score this season but with a couple of near-misses to his name, what Oli McBurnie has thus far lacked in goal contributions he has more than made up for with selfless graft and off-the-ball grunt work, making a total mockery of Steve Clarke’s decision not to include him in Scotland’s World Cup squad. The Hull striker ought to prove a real handful for a decidedly porous home defence, and a goal would be a fitting way to mark a century of Premier League appearances. Chelsea have not won any of their past four league matches against promoted opposition and given Hull’s blistering start to the season, victory on Saturday seems anything but a foregone conclusion.Barry GlendenningChelsea v Hull, Saturday 3pm (all times BST)Chart showing duels won in the Premier League in 2026‑272Arbeloa must trust process as Iraola once didThis might be an opportune moment for Álvaro Arbeloa to meet Andoni Iraola, though perhaps not his Liverpool team. With three defeats from his first three Premier League games as Fulham head coach, and seven goals conceded, questions are already being asked over the former Liverpool defender’s ambitious approach. Just as they were when Iraola failed to win any of his first nine league games in charge ofBournemouth. Trust yourself and the process, might be the Liverpool head coach’s advice if asked. Fulham have been creative under Arbeloa but are easily exposed defensively. Liverpool, starting to click in attack under their new manager, have the assets to exploit Fulham’s weaknesses and subject Arbeloa to an uncomfortable Anfield return. Iraola’s wide options could be reduced, however, with Bradley Barcola suffering cramp on Wednesday – his first start since France’s World Cup semi-final loss – and Cody Gakpo nursing a minor injury.Andy HunterLiverpool v Fulham, Saturday 3pm3Doucouré eagerly waiting Palace returnCheick Doucouré has had a rotten run of luck with injuries. Just when the Mali midfielder looked as if he was ready to make a firstCrystal Palaceappearance since January 2025 in Tuesday’s Carabao Cup win over Middlesbrough, he was taken ill. Pierre Sage revealed last week that Doucouré looked as if he had “given him one million dollars” when he was informed he would be part of the matchday squad at Fulham, where Palace got off the mark with a 3-2 victory. Sage has confirmed that the 26-year-old, who has been sidelined with two serious knee injuries but was once a transfer target for Liverpool, could be involved against Ipswich at Selhurst Park on Saturday. Whenever he does return it is sure to be a heartwarming moment.Ed AaronsCrystal Palace v Ipswich, Saturday 3pmView image in fullscreenCheick Doucouré returned to the Crystal Palace squad for last weekend’s trip to Fulham.Photograph: James Fearn/Getty Images4Cherries must end late lapsesThe midfield battle betweenBrentfordand Bournemouth will be crucial on Saturday with Vitaly Janelt and Mamadou Sangaré setting the tempo for Keith Andrews’ physical side. Brentford top the Premier League for aerial duels won (22.3 per 90 mins), interceptions (11.3 per 90), and fouls committed (16.3 per 90). “They defend well as a team, their high pressing is good,” said Bournemouth’s Marco Rose, who is hoping to guide his side to a first Premier League victory of the season. “Their transition, they have fast players. They have quality everywhere on the pitch, and every situation.” Rose’s answer for Brentford’s aggressiveness should be Alex Scott, who leads his team for interceptions and has drawn nine fouls so far this campaign – the fourth-highest tally in the league. Late drama could also be the deciding factor at the Vitality Stadium. Despite leading in all three of their opening league fixtures, Bournemouth have picked up just two points and four of their five goals conceded have arrived from the 84th minute onwards. History favours their opponents too, as the Cherries have failed to win any of their eight top-flight meetings with the Bees.Yara El-ShabouryBournemouth v Brentford, Saturday 3pmChart showing Premier League stats per game in 2026-27 for aerial duels won, fouls and interceptions5Jackson ready to fill Watkins’ Villa bootsA summer of change at Aston Villa inevitably prompted plenty of noise but most of their new signings were long-standing targets, none more so than Nicolas Jackson. Unai Emery kickstarted Jackson’s career at Villarreal and after reuniting at Villa, the Senegal striker registered hisfirst goal at Club Bruggeon Tuesday after his initial £47.5m move. Jackson has replaced Ollie Watkins, who proved a reliable source of goals across six straight top-flight seasons, and the early evidence has been encouraging. “I had a couple of fights with him when he was at Chelsea so when he first came in I thought: ‘What’s he going to be like?’ but he’s a brilliant guy,” said the Villa captain, John McGinn. “There’s a lot of expectation with the transfer fee but he’s going to be a huge player for us.”Ben FisherAston Villa vNottingham Forest, Saturday 3pm6Signs of early season panic at SpursOnly the most pessimistic home fans at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium will be gripped by anything resembling the kind of dread, anxiety and outright terror that accompaniedEverton’s visit on the final day of last season, but the return of David Moyes’ side so early in the current campaign will still make for nervous viewing. With no goals and just one point on the board after three league games, fan faith in Roberto De Zerbi – and the hundreds of millions of pounds lavished upon new signings – has created a prevailing presumption that Tottenham will soon start firing on at least some, if not all, cylinders. In Everton, Spurs welcome a team whose record in this corner of north London is worse than any other top-flight side. Should they fail to beat a team who have taken just seven points from the past 51 available to them away at Tottenham, the sounds of early but outright mutiny are likely to be audible from the stands.BGTottenham vEverton, Saturday 5.30pmChart showing expected goals per non-penalty shot in 2026-277Stadium of Light to give Guimarães hot receptionOld acquaintance will be renewed at the Stadium of Light on Saturday evening. While Sunderland’s captain and midfield anchor, Granit Xhaka, needs no introduction to his former north London public, the home centre-half Dan Ballard is a former Arsenal youth captain who joined the Gunners’ academy at the age of eight. Then there is Bruno Guimarães. Newcastle’s former captain can expect a hot reception as his new side aim to extend their season-opening run of five straight wins (including the Community Shield). “Arsenal are flying, they’re one of the best teams in Europe,” says Régis Le Bris, Sunderland’s manager. “It will be challenging but I’m very excited to experience this situation again.” Thanks to goals from Ballard and Brian Brobbey, Le Bris choreographed a2-2 Premier League drawagainst Mikel Arteta’s side on Wearside last November. “When you face a strong opponent you can become a bit shy but the most important thing is to be ourselves,” says Le Bris. “Arsenal are so adaptive they will find solutions, so we must be flexible.”Louise TaylorSunderland v Arsenal, Saturday 8pmView image in fullscreenBruno Guimarães returns to the northeast as Arsenal visit Sunderland on Saturday night.Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty Images8Coventry adding points to performances?One of three teams, along with Aston Villa and Tottenham, yet to score a top-flight goal this season, Coventry were extremely unfortunate not to break their duck atManchester Citylast weekend. Having narrowly avoided handing Frank Lampard’s side an early opener, it took a string of excellent saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma to ensure City took three points at the death. “They played really well against Manchester City and created a lot of chances,” said Fabian Hürzeler, who takes his Brighton team to the CBS Arena on Sunday afternoon. Having been scathing in his criticism of his own side’s lack of energy and intensity in their woeful first-half performance against Leeds, the German will be aware that a similarly lethargic performance from his team is unlikely to go unpunished. Particularly away from home against a promoted team that may be firing blanks, but visibly grew in confidence with each passing minute of their defeat to one of the league’s best teams.BGCoventry v Brighton, Sunday 2pmChart showing goals below expected goals in 2026-279Contrasting Manchester teams face off in derbyManchester derby No 199 features a fascinating showdown between two young managers operating in the sport’s rarefied air: Michael Carrick, 45, who bids to guide Manchester United to an 82nd victory in the fixture, and Enzo Maresca, 46, who aims for Manchester City’s 63rd. As the great Pep Guardiola’s successor, the visiting Italian can be delighted at his team’s perfect record from their four games under him since the Community Shield. Carrick, though, should be disappointed at the return from an opening three matches as United’s permanent manager: adefeat at Hullanddraw at Everton, with the5-2 home win over Ipswichsandwiched between. United fans will protest beforehand about the club’s approach to eradicating ticket touting, the occasion should be particularly spicy and vibrant.Jamie JacksonManchester United v Manchester City, Sunday 4.30pmView image in fullscreenManchester United supporters protested ticket touts earlier in the season and will do so again before the Manchester derby.Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters10Battle of the goalkeepers at Elland RoadTwo teams unbeaten in the Premier League this season, two German managers in the dugouts and a Monday night goalkeeping beauty contest at Elland Road. While Daniel Farke welcomes his compatriot, Matthias Jaissle, to West Yorkshire for the first time, James Trafford – the £40m England keeper Newcastle tried to sign on three separate occasions – will be in goal for Leeds. The visitors eventually turned their attentions to the £26m Czechia goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who arrived on Tyneside from Braga in July. So far at least, Jaissle is delighted by the 24-year-old’s performances. “Lukas is an amazing signing who has been amazing,” said Eddie Howe’s successor. “Coming to the Premier League and dealing with the pressure is not easy and, as a keeper, that pressure is something else. I like Lukas a lot. He’s so calm but so mature as well. There’s not even a hint of nervousness. He gives the whole team confidence. That helps a lot.”LTLeeds v Newcastle, Monday 8pmPosTeamPGDPts1Man City3592Arsenal3593Hull3374Chelsea3165Brentford3356Liverpool3257Newcastle3258Everton3259Leeds31510Brighton33411Man Utd31412Sunderland30413Crystal Palace3-4314Ipswich3-4315AFC Bournemouth3-1216Nottm Forest3-1217Aston Villa3-5118Tottenham Hotspur3-5119Fulham3-3020Coventry3-50Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueTen things to look out for this weekendManchester CityArsenalHull CityChelseaBrentfordLiverpoolfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Sesko soars as Manchester United surge past Sabah on Champions League return | Champions League | The Guardian
description: Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez were also on target in Manchester United’s 4-0 win against Sabah in the Champions League
Author: David Hytner
Headline: Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez were also on target in Manchester United’s 4-0 win against Sabah in the Champions League
Content: Benjamin Sesko celebrates after scoring Manchester United’s third goal before half-time.Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenBenjamin Sesko celebrates after scoring Manchester United’s third goal before half-time.Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/ReutersChampions LeagueSesko soars as Manchester United surge past Sabah on Champions League returnDavid Hytnerat Old TraffordThu 10 Sep 2026 17.05 EDTLast modified on Thu 10 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIt was a night for romance given the astonishing story that Sabah brought with them to Old Trafford for their Champions League debut. This is a club that did not even exist a decade ago and nobody saw their bolt to the title in Azerbaijan coming last season; in 2024-25, they had finished 41 points off the top. The job that their manager, Valdas Dambrauskas,has done since taking overin the summer of last year is extraordinary.It was also a night for cold, hard reality.Manchester Unitedwere back in Europe’s elite competition after a two-year hiatus and in need of something to soothe them after the trauma of their last-gasp coughing up of two points in last Sunday’s Premier League draw at Everton. And before the extremely serious business of the derby here against Manchester City on Sunday. They got it on the back of a first-half performance that burned slowly before catching fire.Sabah were game. United were clinical. It was Matheus Cunha who broke the deadlock midway through the first half and the defining moments came at the end of the period when Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko sent United into half-time with a three-goal cushion. Lisandro Martínez added the fourth late on. It was a case of job done for Michael Carrick, no wobbles. Now for City.Mickels miss a turning point as latest stop in Sabah’s odyssey ends with regret | Jamie JacksonRead moreUnited had wanted to put their best foot forward when they heard theChampions Leaguearia after the chaos and embarrassment of their previous involvement in the competition. Erik ten Hag was the manager in 2023-24 and his team finished bottom of their group with four points, starting and ending with losses to Bayern Munich. It was what happened in between times against Galatasaray and Copenhagen that still causes a few shudders. It was a period when United panicked uncontrollably when they had a lead. When the defensive gifts from them came in crazy clusters.Carrick took no chances with his starting XI. There was minimal rotation in the midfield and front line, save for a first start of the season for Sesko in the No 9 position. It was easy to think that the manager wanted to groove Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo in central midfield before the City game.United looked to Fernandes to get them going. As always. There were intelligent runs from him; incision about his passes, that wonderful disguise on some of them. The breakthrough goal stemmed from him chasing a high ball over the top that looked like a lost cause only for him to keep it in play. It was what happened next that quickened United pulses. When Sabah gave the ball away cheaply to Bryan Mbeumo, United moved quickly over to the left. Patrick Dorgu crossed and Cunha’s finish was clean.Quick GuideGabriel, 15, stars with hat-trick for United in Youth League debutShowManchester United's JJ Gabriel (pictured) marked his Uefa Youth League debut with a hat-trick against Sabah aged just 15. The attacker is tipped as a future star and made his first appearance for the first team off the bench in last month’s friendly against Atlético Madrid.Gabriel has yet to make Michael Carrick’s squad for a competitive match but the teenager, who turns 16 next month, continues to knock on the door. He sparkled for the Under-19s in Thursday’s 5-0 win against Sabah in the Youth League in front of director of football Jason Wilcox, director of recruitment Christopher Vivell and first-team coach Travis Binnion.Amir Ibragimov and Jacob Watson scored early goals in Leigh, where Gabriel added another in a dominant first half.Gabriel scored two more late in the second half to claim the match ball against the Azerbaijani visitors, who did not manage a shot on a day that United mustered 44 attempts.PAPhotograph: Zohaib Alam/Manchester UnitedWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Sabah lined up in a 4-3-3 formation; no bus parking. They wanted to ask questions of a United defence that had a makeshift feel about it. There was assurance on the ball from them, the desire to carry it forward. And a huge chance in the 35th minute when Kaheem Parris crossed to the back post. Joy-Lance Mickels was clear of Noussair Mazraoui only to put the header wide. The angle was not favourable. It did not entirely excuse him.View image in fullscreenMatheus Cunha opens the scoring with a smart finish in the first half.Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty ImagesSabah were harshly treated by the half-time scoreline, even though United played on the front foot and created openings. It was the one-two punch in the closing stages of the first period that changed everything. Fernandes – who else? – made a sidefoot finish look easy after Tielemans had burst on a Cunha pass inside, spun and teed him up. The third followed a first time pass by Fernandes into Mbeumo, who got Sesko clean though. The Sabah backline was high. Sesko went around the goalkeeper to score. He never looked like missing.There was a lovely scene 90 ­minutes before kick-off when some of the Sabah players wandered around the pitch, the stadium virtually empty, phones out to capture the quiet before the storm, the sheer scale of Old Trafford. They wore wide smiles. They were determined not to be overawed when it got started. The performance of the strolling central midfielder, Ivan Lepinjica, was certainly impressive. They were just too loose at the back.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionUnited played some slick stuff at times, Mainoo and ­Fernandes ever involved. When Carrick’s ­pass-and-move game clicks, it is easy to feel the ­possibility. ­Imposing it against the higher-­profile teams is the name of the game. ­Starting against City.Fenerbahce coach resigns after draw with Roma – but president insists he will stayRead moreMason Mount was introduced at half-time for his first football of the season – “It was great to get Mason back on the pitch,” Carrick later said – with Tielemans coming off, his work done. The Belgian could be pleased with his impact. Carrick was always going to withdraw other likely starters against City, such as Mainoo. Sesko came off with him on 64 minutes and was warmly applauded. After his goal at Everton on Sunday, has he done enough to make the XI for the derby?Carrick added: “We always push for more. Results-wise it hasn’t been the start we wanted, but performance-wise there are a lot of things we were looking for. The clean sheet was important tonight. Collectively as a team we have done a lot of good things and that is why we are excited what this season can bring.”His side controlled the second half. The jeopardy was long gone. The fourth goal summed up Sabah’s travails in their defensive third. It was a scooped free-kick by Fernandes for Joshua Zirkzee, on as a substitute, and when his backheel hit Aden ­McCarthy, the Sabah goalkeeper, Stas Pokatilov, lost his bearings, the ball caught under his feet. It was a tap-in for Martínez. The substitute, Orphé Mbina, headed high for Sabah at the very end. There was to be no fairytale goal.Explore more on these topicsChampions LeagueManchester UnitedSabahEuropean club footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Angel Reese and Caitlin Clark celebrate their ‘chemistry’ as USA advance to Fiba World Cup semis | Fiba Women's Basketball World Cup 2026 | The Guardian
description: A United States team full of WNBA stars breezed into the semi-finals of the Women’s Basketball World Cup with a 108-56 win against Hungary on Thursday
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: A United States team full of WNBA stars breezed into the semi-finals of the Women’s Basketball World Cup with a 108-56 win against Hungary on Thursday
Content: Angel Reese and Caitlin Clark helped the US through to the Fiba World Cup semi-finals.Photograph: Christina Pahnke/sampics/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAngel Reese and Caitlin Clark helped the US through to the Fiba World Cup semi-finals.Photograph: Christina Pahnke/sampics/Getty ImagesFiba Women's Basketball World Cup 2026Angel Reese and Caitlin Clark celebrate their ‘chemistry’ as USA advance to Fiba World Cup semisFiba World Cup: USA 108-56 HungaryReese and Clark have been portrayed as fierce rivalsAgenciesThu 10 Sep 2026 08.25 EDTLast modified on Thu 10 Sep 2026 12.18 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAngel Reese and Caitlin Clark’ s interactions are a subplot of the women’s Fiba World Cup, the WNBA season and if you spend enough time on social media,a divided United States. Clark and Reese have shown their relationship on the court is thriving, and they both excelled in USA’s 108-56 quarter-final win over Hungary on Thursday.In Thursday’s game, the growing chemistry showed. The pair had a nifty pick-and-roll to end the first quarter that ended with a layup by Reese. The Atlanta Dream forward returned the favor hitting Clark on a fastbreak for an easy lay-up later in the game.Angel Reese is turning trolls and talk of ‘mebounds’ into fuel for a breakthroughRead more“She’s got it for me a lot of times so it’s probably finally due for me to get one to her and she easily finished it,” Reese said smiling.Napheesa Collier was USA’s top-scorer with 19 points, Clark delivered nine assists and added 10 points, while Reese had six rebounds and nine points in a dominant quarter-final performance. The Americans, who are chasing a fifth consecutive World Cup title, will face either Spain or Australia in the semi-finals on Saturday.Clark and Reese are intense and animated competitors, and their fan bases’ are fiercely loyal. On much of social media fans are either for Reese or for Clark. But the pair have bonded so far at the World Cup. Clark said many of the stories about their relationship are “false takes,” saying she loves the fiery competitiveness that she and Reese share.“No matter what, there’s always going to be people that create those narratives and say whatever they want to say,” Clark said. “There’s definitely no stopping that and they’re always going to be there. I think for ourselves, like I said, it’s easy for us to just come in here and compete.”Reese has enjoyed playing with Clark as well as the other young members of the roster, including Paige Bueckers and Aliyah Boston.“We know each other’s game like the back of each other’s hand, she knows my spots,” Reese said of Clark. “We just continue to build chemistry because we know we’re going to be USA teammates for a while.”Clark laughed recalling one incident in the tournament between she and Reese that has gotten some attention. When Clark was subbing in during the opener against China and started to step on the court before being officially told to, Reese, who was entering the game at the same time, pulled her back off the court.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“Well, the ref had gotten mad at me a couple of times prior, so she was saving me from the ref getting mad at me again,” Clark said, laughing.The pair will be back on opposite sides soon enough – Reese’s Atlanta Dream and Clark’s Indiana Fever are headed for the WNBA playoffs and both have 26-14 records. They could meet in the first round if the current seeds hold.Explore more on these topicsFiba Women's Basketball World Cup 2026USA women's basketball teamCaitlin ClarkBasketballUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Brave new world: Ultimate Championship brings glowing javelins and $10m prize fund to track and field | Athletics | The Guardian
description: New event aims to revolutionise the sport with promises of bigger prize money and a greater role for athletes
Author: Sean Ingle
Headline: New event aims to revolutionise the sport with promises of bigger prize money and a greater role for athletes
Content: Noah Lyles at the Ultimate Championship’s launch, where he enjoyed a stint as a DJ.Photograph: Dénes Erdős/APView image in fullscreenNoah Lyles at the Ultimate Championship’s launch, where he enjoyed a stint as a DJ.Photograph: Dénes Erdős/APAthleticsBrave new world: Ultimate Championship brings glowing javelins and $10m prize fund to track and fieldNew event aims to revolutionise the sport with promises of bigger prize money and a greater role for athletesSean Inglein BudapestThu 10 Sep 2026 13.30 EDTLast modified on Thu 10 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTrack and field’s brave new world begins in Budapest on Friday night. The action will be fast-paced and slick, with augmented reality showing athletes’ win percentages and javelins and hammers that glow, making them easier to see on a black infield. In the space of 48 hours, a top sprinter could earn $337,500 (£250,000) for just over a minute’s work.It is all part of the newWorld AthleticsUltimate Championship, a three-day event with a prize fund of $10m which is designed to pit the best against the best, and kick off a minor revolution in the sport.‘I’m not a robot’: Josh Kerr primed to peak against arch rival IngebrigtsenRead moreWhen Usain Bolt, who is a global ambassador for the event, was told that anyone who wins the 100m, 200m and mixed 4x100m relay here will walk away £250,000 richer, he smiled – and recalled a conversation he had just recently had with another legendary Jamaican sprinter, Asafa Powell.“I was chatting to Asafa before I came here and we were like: ‘Jeez, we missed out on a big cash prize,’” he said. “I won a fair few championships and it still doesn’t add up to all that cash. I am sad I missed out on it, but I’m happy for the athletes.”The idea is the brainchild of WorldAthleticspresident, Sebastian Coe, and chief executive, Jon Ridgeon. But this is just the start of plans to make the sport richer – and more popular.“We will deliver magnetic indelible moments that will travel around all four corners of the globe, and I think we will see a compelling glimpse into the future and the potential of this sport, which at its best is untouchable,” said Coe.“We also want this championship to be an incubator for change. As a proud Sheffielder, I would describe it as a blast furnace, ultimately shaping what our sport will look like going forward. And we want to take some of these innovations into the world championships and Olympic Games.”View image in fullscreenKeely Hodgkinson savours the red carpet treatment.Photograph: Ben Stansall/AFP/Getty ImagesSo what could be next? The Guardian can reveal there is growing clamour for Coe to stay on at WorldAthleticsin some capacity when his presidency ends in September 2027. One plan being discussed is for Coe to lead a new commercial arm, which aims to sell World Athletics’ own rights for the first time and add substantial external investment and revenues.Such a move could come about because at the end of 2029, World Athletics’ commercial contract with the sports marketing agency Dentsu, which is worth around £14m a year, will end.While it has been a happy relationship, the current deal means that even if World Athletics wants to use footage from its own world championships at its own awards ceremony it has to pay Dentsu.But in three years’ time World Athletics will have control of its commercial and broadcast rights for the first time in three decades, allowing it to explore fresh options on how best to fund the sport.It is understood that Coe, who has transformed the governance and fortunes of World Athletics since taking over from the corrupt Lamine Diack regime in 2015, is undecided as to whether he would take on such a role.In a statement to the Guardian, World Athletics said: “At the end of 2029, most of World Athletics’ commercial contracts and broadcast relationships will come to an end, as will our current contract with Dentsu, who has owned our commercial rights since 2014, and we will be in a position to sell our own rights from 2030 onwards.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenBritain’s Amy Hunt poses for a photo after the lane draft for the women’s 200m semi-finals.Photograph: Shaun Botterill/Getty Images“With that in mind, our executive board has spent the last 18 months looking at the commercial structures we need to create and determining the best way to increase revenue so we can accelerate growth in our sport over the coming years.“We are making consequential progress in an area that obviously requires detailed consultation throughout our organisation and across our sport.”Another sign of athletics’ strength is that the BBC has significantly scaled up its operation here because the viewing figures were so strong at the European championships, with more than four million watching at peak times.In total 381 top athletes from 65 federations will compete in Budapest, with the winner of each race getting $150,000 and even the eighth-place finisher walking away with $10,000.Another change is that athletes have been involved in the planning and presentation of the event, with the Olympic 100m champion, Noah Lyles, even acting as a DJ. It started with a red carpet introduction on Thursday with several athletes, including the pole vault star Mondo Duplantis and 800m Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson, wearing jackets and dresses that wouldn’t have been out of place at the Oscars.One sign of the relaxed atmosphere came when Hodgkinson was asked by a member of the press whether she was 100% fit after a minor hamstring niggle at the European championships in Birmingham. “None of your business,” she replied, smiling.Explore more on these topicsAthleticsSebastian CoeWorld AthleticsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Maye’s ‘unacceptable’ trio of interceptions help Seahawks win season opener over Pats | NFL | The Guardian
description: Drew Lock stepped in for an injured Sam Darnold as Seattle rallied from 10 points down to beat New England 13-10 on banner night
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Drew Lock stepped in for an injured Sam Darnold as Seattle rallied from 10 points down to beat New England 13-10 on banner night
Content: Josh Jobe of the Seattle Seahawks intercepts a pass intended for New England Patriots receiver Mack Hollins in the end zone during the fourth quarter at Lumen Field in Seattle.Photograph: Jane Gershovich/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJosh Jobe of the Seattle Seahawks intercepts a pass intended for New England Patriots receiver Mack Hollins in the end zone during the fourth quarter at Lumen Field in Seattle.Photograph: Jane Gershovich/Getty ImagesNFLMaye’s ‘unacceptable’ trio of interceptions help Seahawks win season opener over PatsNew England Patriots 10-13 Seattle SeahawksBackup quarterback engineers late Seattle rallySam Darnold exits opening drive with hip injuryAgenciesThu 10 Sep 2026 07.29 EDTFirst published on Thu 10 Sep 2026 00.00 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBackup quarterback Drew Lock led two late scoring drives and the Seattle Seahawks intercepted Drake Maye three times in the fourth quarter to overcome an early injury to starter Sam Darnold and beat theNew England Patriots13-10 on Wednesday night in a Super Bowl rematch.The Seahawks were held to just a field goal through three quarters as Lock and the offense struggled to move the ball after Darnold injured his hip on the opening drive.ESPN reportsthat he could return for Seattle’s Week 3 game against the Washington Commanders.“At this point, we are able to rule out a fracture,” Seattle head coach Mike Macdonald said after the game. “So there’s some more tests to be done. ... We’re still working through all that, but right now I think fracture is out, which is great news.”NFL 2026 season predictions: which teams can bring down the Rams juggernaut?Read moreThe costly interceptions by last season’s MVP runner-up turned the tide and made sure that the banner-raising night would end in happy fashion for the boisterous home crowd.Maye overcame the first two picks to drive the Patriots into position to tie or take the lead in the final minute. But Josh Jobe made a toe-tapping interception in the end zone to seal the win.“I thought we had a good plan to try to start chipping away and be patient. Lost patience and it cost us – decisions that cost us the game on my part, on my end,” Maye said. “I vow to myself to be better and realize it’s a long season. But at the same time, you can’t have those. It’s unacceptable.”Seattle trailed 10-0 but got a field goal in the third quarter and tied the game when Lock connected with Jaxon Smith-Njigba on a 45-yard pass on fourth-and-1 following an interception by Nehemiah Pritchett.Julian Love intercepted Maye on the next drive and the Seahawks took a 13-10 lead on a 26-yard field goal by Jason Myers. That set the stage for the defensive stand on the final drive.The game started following a ceremony that featured the Super Bowl banner being raised and highlights being played on the video board. This was the third Super Bowl rematch in Week 1, with it last happening in 2016 when Denver celebrated their title with a win over Carolina.The excitement turned to worry quickly as Darnold came up limping following a third-down sack by Dre’Mont Jones on the first drive. Darnold went immediately to the sideline medical tent and then back to the locker room before the next drive.Lock, who threw just three passes last season, entered the game but Seattle’s offense was stagnant until the fourth quarter.The Patriots didn’t fare much better on offense but got the only score of the first half after Jobe interfered with offseason acquisition AJ Brown on a deep flea-flicker pass and Maye found rookie Eli Raridon for a two-yard score on the next play to make it 7-0.A penalty helped set up the second Patriots score as well. Chazz Surratt was flagged for roughing the punter on the opening drive of the second half, setting up Andy Borregales’ 50-yard field goal.Explore more on these topicsNFLSeattle SeahawksNew England PatriotsUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Hamilton confirms no rules of engagement at Ferrari despite Monza clash with Leclerc | Formula One 2026 | The Guardian
description: Lewis Hamilton stated Ferrari ‘needs to probably change’ its stance on having no rules of engagement between its drivers
Author: Giles Richards
Headline: Lewis Hamilton stated Ferrari ‘needs to probably change’ its stance on having no rules of engagement between its drivers
Content: Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton (left) and teammate Charles Leclerc come together into the first chicane at the Italian Grand Prix.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAView image in fullscreenFerrari’s Lewis Hamilton (left) and teammate Charles Leclerc come together into the first chicane at the Italian Grand Prix.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAFormula One 2026Hamilton confirms no rules of engagement at Ferrari despite Monza clash with Leclerc‘When I was at Mercedes we had written rules’British driver held positive talks with teammateGiles Richardsat the MadringThu 10 Sep 2026 12.12 EDTLast modified on Thu 10 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLewis Hamilton has said there remain no rules of engagement between the drivers at Ferrari, despite the 41-year-old calling for the team to employ them after he clashed with his teammate,Charles Leclerc, at the last round in Monza.Hamilton was forced wide by Leclerc at turn two on the opening lap at the Italian Grand Prix, which he felt had been unacceptable. Speaking before the first meeting for the Spanish Grand Prix at the new Madring circuit in Madrid this weekend, Leclerc admitted he had been at fault and Hamilton said the pair had talked frankly and cleared the air in a forthright fashion.‘Like an AI agent’: Wolff hails Antonelli’s Italian GP victory in title chargeRead moreIn Monza Hamilton had unfavourably comparedFerrarito his former team Mercedes, stating: “When I was at Mercedes we had written rules of engagement. Here there are no rules. That’s something that needs to probably change.”Hamilton noted that he had positive discussions with the team principal, Fred Vasseur, but when asked if there was an agreement on rules of engagement between the two drivers, he was unequivocal. “There was not,” he said. “I’m sure at some stage we’ll discuss how we can be better, but we’ve not had a lot of time to just turn around. You can’t change things in two days.”The seven-time champion said in Monza he believed Leclerc had forced him off track and pointedly noted that he had always tried to race cleanly. In Madrid Leclerc took responsibility for what happened. “I obviously know I went too far in turn two,” he said. “I said it to Lewis and I think it’s very clear what we should do or should avoid going forward.”Hamilton praised his teammate’s attitude in clearing up the issues. “What’s great is that there was no shying away from having a discussion,” he said. “We sat face to face, just him and I, talked about it and we were just both open and honest. We squashed it and we can move on.View image in fullscreenLewis Hamilton speaks to the media in Madrid.Photograph: David Davies/PA“That shows the maturity from him. I think it’s healthy. It’s a relationship we have built over time. I’m sure there’ll be more times where we’re close because we’re very close in pace. We both want to win just as much as each other and we both want to do well for the team as well. But it’s real positive.”The race in Monza was won byMercedes’ Kimi Antonelli, who now leads Hamilton, who is third in the championship, by 76 points, a gap the British driver concededwas all but unbridgeable. He had also called on Ferrari to make changes to sharpen procedures and execution, operationally and strategically, after Monza to maximise potential points but conceded that it would not be achievable overnight.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“It’s a longer term process, it’s not something we can just change into this weekend,” Hamilton said. “There’s a huge amount of moving parts, there’s a lot of people, there’s a culture that’s been there for a long, long time and moving big pieces is not so easy.“It starts with the acknowledgment which internally we have and so then it just comes to working out the solutions together and it just doesn’t happen overnight. We’ll probably try things and it still won’t be good, but we’ll eventually get to the point we need.”Explore more on these topicsFormula One 2026Lewis HamiltonFerrariCharles LeclercFormula OneMotor sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Saloons, school and specialty coffee: NWSL players enjoy new era of side hustles | NWSL | The Guardian
description: Star players once worked for Amazon or DoorDash to make ends meet on meager salaries. A new CBA opened doors for off-field pursuits in line with their passions
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Star players once worked for Amazon or DoorDash to make ends meet on meager salaries. A new CBA opened doors for off-field pursuits in line with their passions
Content: In the past year, Bea Franklin’s work has taken her to finance offices, a country-themed Idaho saloon and the soccer field with the Chicago Stars.Photograph: Daniel Bartel/NWSL/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenIn the past year, Bea Franklin’s work has taken her to finance offices, a country-themed Idaho saloon and the soccer field with the Chicago Stars.Photograph: Daniel Bartel/NWSL/Getty ImagesNWSLSaloons, school and specialty coffee: NWSL players enjoy new era of side hustlesFive years ago, stars in the league packed Amazon boxes or drove for DoorDash to make ends meet on meager salaries. A new CBA opened doors for off-field pursuits in line with their passionsRoey HadarThu 10 Sep 2026 06.00 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOn a cold winter night in Ketchum, Idaho, Chicago Stars midfielder Bea Franklin was pulling off a different sort of physical feat than what she usually does on the soccer field. Under the eyes of taxidermied animals at the Pioneer Saloon, she deftly balanced martinis as a cocktail waitress, wearing cowgirl boots and ensuring the olives didn’t drip when she walked down stairs.Franklin did not take a second job as a cocktail waitress in a Rocky Mountain ski resort town not out of necessity, but as a way to think about more than just the sport that has dominated much of her life.“It was just so much fun, and a really great way to kind of disconnect from soccer,” Franklin said.‘The heartbeat of game day’: how NWSL fans in Boston built culture from the ground upRead moreHardly half a decade ago, a player like Franklin, a 25-year-old in her third pro season, might have needed a job like this just to get by.Five years ago this summer, NWSL players organizedthe “No More Side Hustles” campaignto highlight the league’s low pay and the need for players to get second jobs while playing, training and working as full-time professional athletes.At the time, a third of the NWSL Players Association’s members made the league minimum salary of $22,000; 75% made $31,000 or less. Jessica McDonald, a World Cup winner,workedat Amazon packing boxes for 10 hours a day while running training sessions for young players at night. Kristen Hamilton, a three-time league champion,drovefor DoorDash. Others cleaned homes, worked as receptionists or mopped floors.It spoke to a major problem that the league has, by and large, addressed successfully. The NWSLPA agreed to its first collective bargaining agreement with the league in 2022. Under the current CBA, reached in 2024, the minimum salary for players is $50,500 for the 2026 season – nearly the same amount as the maximum in 2021 ($52,500).Now, with the security of a living wage, players are free to take on academic, professional and entrepreneurial pursuits. Not because they have to, but because theywantto.Washington Spirit defender Gabrielle Carle is working on becoming a doctor after her playing career wraps. She said she briefly considered doing both until realizing that was too ambitious, even for her.“I was like, ‘Oh, this is gonna be complicated,’” Carle said. “These two don’t really work together.”View image in fullscreenDuring the Washington Spirit’s run to the NWSL final last season, starting defender Gabrielle Carle was also studying for the MCAT.Photograph: Hannah Foslien/NWSL/Getty ImagesNevertheless, Carle was not deterred. During the 2025 season, a career year for the full-back from Quebec, she studied during the season for the MCAT and then took the exam in January. The 27-year-old said she passed the score she hoped to reach and plans to take advantage of the three-year window to use the score in a medical school application.“I’m going to be 30 years old. I can decide if that’s a good time for me to retire or if I want to keep going. But if I do decide to move on with my career and retire from soccer, then I have that score and I can immediately move on to the next part of my life,” Carle said.Even with a few years between a decision about medical school, Carle has relished the chance to do more than just play soccer and keep herself in what she dubbed her “smart mode”. She is applying for positions where she can conduct sports medicine research.Carle is not the only player to juggle scouting reports with schoolbooks. Her Washington Spirit teammate, Lucia Di Guglielmo, has a master’s degree in industrial chemistry. In England, Chelsea captain Erin Cuthbert hasearnedher MBA, while Manchester United goalkeeper Phallon Tullis-Joyce put her degree in marine biology to use byhostingstudents for workshops at a local zoo.This year, the NWSL and Syracuse Universitylauncheda partnership that allows players to pursue online degrees and certificates in programs ranging from sports analytics and cybersecurity to business management and accounting.Franklin, who studied finance at the University of Arkansas, took a job last season at Bank of America as a wealth management analyst on afternoons after training and on her off days and helping manage the investments of some extremely wealthy clients. She felt that the skills she learned are helpful for someone like her, even if, as she readily concedes, she does not fall into that income bracket.“It puts some real-world application into how people get credit and actually going through banking process or, even just seeing the nitty-gritty of opening a bank account on the other side,” Franklin said. “And now, when I do it again, I’ll have a bit more patience for the person on the other end of the phone, because that was me sometimes.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionSeveral players have gone further by starting businesses of their own. This summer, two NWSL players on the Canadian national team launched businesses: Chicago forward Jordyn Huitema started Jordyskin, a skincare line, and Denver Summit full-back Janine Sonis created 90Brew, a specialty coffee brand.Coffee has been a frequent jumping-off point for soccer players looking to go entrepreneurial: Cuthbert has acoffee brand called Ruby Alba; England legend Jill Scott createdBoxx2Boxx coffee shopin Manchester; and a group of Kansas City Current teammates openedPitchside Coffee.Sonis launched her business in the middle of a career year on the field, where she has scored nine goals for the Summit in their expansion season.Earlier this month, 90Brew started taking its first orders. Sonis said it was part of a tumultuous 18-month process tied to a lingering problem early in her pro soccer career.“I actually started drinking coffee because, funny enough, I couldn’t stay awake,” Sonis said.A self-described coffee fanatic, Sonis followed the lead of her husband Ethan, who launched an athletic training business in 2018. A joking conversation with a friend after the 2024 season became serious when her husband asked her why she would not just go for it and start the business.Janine Sonis: ‘63,000 fans in Denver proves a women’s team was way overdue’Read moreSonis was quick to credit the support network she has had in starting the business. In a turn from the days when teams were indifferent or even hostile to players in the years before the league instituted major reforms, she said that her club has been immensely supportive. It doesn’t hurt that, independently of each other, the Summit and 90Brew share similar shades of green.“We picked those colors before the logo for the Summit had come out, which is really funny and just really kind of validated what we were doing,” she said. “I remember the moment that the logo came out for the Summit and I’m like, ‘You’ve gotta be kidding me.’”The 32-year-old Sonis is a full decade removed from her NWSL debut. She knew the darker days of side hustles and second jobs. For her, it is a full-circle moment, and a sign of just how far the league has come.“Even really not that far in the past, which is crazy that people had to have two jobs and their NWSL salaries weren’t supporting them enough not to have to do something else,” she said. “And now here I am being able to support myself in multiple ventures because of the direction that the game has moved in.”Explore more on these topicsNWSLWomen's footballfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Why David Beckham will have my vote for the US Soccer Hall of Fame | MLS | The Guardian
description: The Englishman has gotten no shortage of recognition, but his contributions to the American game deserve an official title
Author: Pablo Iglesias Maurer
Headline: The Englishman has gotten no shortage of recognition, but his contributions to the American game deserve an official title
Content: David Beckham has made his mark on US soccer.Composite: AFP/Getty Images; Adidas/EPA; EPAView image in fullscreenDavid Beckham has made his mark on US soccer.Composite: AFP/Getty Images; Adidas/EPA; EPAMLSWhy David Beckham will have my vote for the US Soccer Hall of FamePablo Iglesias MaurerThe Englishman has gotten no shortage of recognition, but his contributions to the American game deserve an official titleSign up for our free newsletter hereThu 10 Sep 2026 10.54 EDTLast modified on Thu 10 Sep 2026 10.56 EDTShareNext spring, when the US Soccer Hall of Fame welcomes its newest class, there will be pomp and circumstance. The hall, which sits in a corner of Toyota Stadium, home of Major League Soccer’s FC Dallas, will feature the enshrineds’ signature red jackets. There will be glad-handing and speeches from players and coaches, misty-eyed reflections on their upbringings and their careers.Many involved will be American-born soccer legends, of course. Yet every once in a while, a player whose footprint extends well beyond the borders of the United States graces the stage. Such may be the case next year when the hall potentially welcomes English legendDavid Beckhaminto the fold.Man City-bound 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan is MLS’s chaotic revelationRead moreSome readers abroad – and certainly plenty of readers here in the States – will wonder why an ostensiblyAmericanHall of Fame would admit non-Americans, something it’s done since its inception. The answer lies in the nature of the American game itself. Even our earliest heroes – Joe Gaetjens and the like – were immigrants, with Gaetjens scoring his famed goal against England in the 1950 World Cup when he wasn’t even a US citizen (he never ended up becoming one).Advance through the decades and big-name, American-born heroes do start to emerge, but they are still outpaced by those from abroad. The history of the North American Soccer League is replete with foreign-born members of the country’s hall of fame such as Pelé, Franz Beckenbauer and Carlos Alberto. Even the MajorIndoorSoccer League got its due eventually: just last year, Steve Zungul, the “lord of all indoors”, was inducted. Tatu, another foreign-born legend of the arena, seems likely to go in this year.All of which is to say, there’s precedent for this. If you made a sizable contribution to soccer in the United States, you’re eligible – period. It’s the way it should be.By that standard, there’s no doubting Beckham’s credentials. Perhaps the most direct analog for his contributions is the career of Pelé, who arrived stateside in 1977 and transformed the landscape of the game in this country. Like Beckham’s stay with the LA Galaxy, the Brazilian’s playing career was successful. He won a league championship in 1977 and was wildly productive throughout the entirety of his stay in the US. He did every interview, signed every autograph, more or less, and went on to found a soccer camp in New Jersey that produced thousands of soccer-mad children, more than one of whom went on to feature for the US men’s national team. He remained a presence for decades after his retirement.Still, after all of that, professional soccer in the US more or less collapsed within seven years of his departure.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMLS’s transfer window and the spending line that keeps going upRead moreBeckham’s playing career with the Galaxy (2007-2012) was in some ways more successful than Pelé’s. Much has been made about his tumultuous arrival in the US, so expertly told by the late, great Grant Wahl in his book The Beckham Experiment.After the smoke cleared, though, Beckham was a mainstay for the Galaxy, working alongside Landon Donovan (a Hall of Famer himself) to lead the club to a pair of league titles and two Supporters’ Shields.His true effect, though, came at a league level. Major League Soccer created an entirely new roster mechanism – the designated player rule – to accommodate Beckham’s arrival, a guideline that fundamentally changed its reality. Like Pelé, scores of uninitiated fans filledMLSstadiums to see Beckham. And just as the Brazilian did, Beckham stayed well beyond the end of his playing days, eventually founding Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami, the current standard bearer of the league.The Hall of Fame inducts candidates in three categories: player, veteran and builder, the last of which is reserved for those whose work was primarily off the field. Beckham’s inclusion this year comes in the veteran category, where he’s nominated alongside nine other deserving candidates. The presence of his name has been the subject of much debate among the hall’s voters, of which I am one.Arguments against his inclusion center on the fact that, in several years, Beckham’s name seems likely to come up on a list of “builder” nominees. Certainly, helping to found Inter Miami, and luring the greatest player in history to play there, is worth considering by that standard. So if he stands a good chance of making it in that way, then why not save this spot for someone else?To me, though, voting him in now is an easy decision – why wait? Beckham’s playing career alone stacks up favorably against many members of the hall. And while he is unquestionably a “builder”, so much of that work was simultaneous with his career as a player.His mere presence on field legitimized a still fledgeling league and led to a decade-long boom that saw it nearly double in size. This, of course, is not solely Beckham’s doing – far from it – but I could easily make an argument that Beckham’s influence on American soccer is as big as Pelé’s – and Pelé, of course, has a place in the hall.So, English-born Beckham will be getting one of my votes for induction. In truth, three of my five selections for induction (Beckham, Tatu, Ken Cooper Sr, Tiffany Roberts and Clint Mathis) are foreign-born. That feels truly American to me.This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US.Subscribe for free here.Explore more on these topicsMLSDavid BeckhamUS sportscommentShareReuse this content

title: Clearlake Capital close on buying out Chelsea co-owners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter | Chelsea | The Guardian
description: The deal would see Todd Boehly and Mark Walter make a profit on their investment and value the club at around £5bn
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: The deal would see Todd Boehly and Mark Walter make a profit on their investment and value the club at around £5bn
Content: Clearlake are already 61.5% shareholders of Chelsea.Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenClearlake are already 61.5% shareholders of Chelsea.Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesChelseaClearlake Capital close on buying out Chelsea co-owners Todd Boehly and Mark WalterDeal would value club at around £5bnWalter is seeking to raise funds to pay off insurersMatt HughesandJacob SteinbergThu 10 Sep 2026 16.49 EDTLast modified on Thu 10 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleChelsea’s majority owners, Clearlake Capital, are closing in on an agreement to buy out co-owners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter in a deal that would see the pair make a profit on their investment and value the club at around £5bn.On-off discussions between the two ownership groups over a potential sale have been taking place for the last two years, but intensified last month as a result of Mark Walter seeking to raise funds to pay off insurers following a US federal investigation over alleged tax fraud.Chelsea’s 2016-17 Premier League title should be given to Spurs, says PochettinoRead moreWalter, Boehly and Swiss billionaire Hansjörg Wyss all own 12.8% of Chelsea following their joint £2.5bn purchase of the club with Clearlake from Roman Abramovich four years ago, in a deal in which the new owners commit to spending a further £1.75bn on the club.Under the terms of their ownership agreement, none of Chelsea’s shareholders can sell to a third party without the consent of their partners giving Clearlake, whose investment is managed by Behdad Eghbali and José E Feliciano, an exclusive option to purchase Boehly and Walter’s stakes.In a statement issued to Bloomberg a spokesperson for Walter confirmed that he is seeking a sale with an agreement close. Boehly is also expected to sell as he is a long-time investment partner of Walters. Wyss’s position is unconfirmed.“This potential transaction values Mark Walter’s stake in Chelsea Football Club at a premium to his initial investment and is another successful sports investment for him,” a spokesperson for Walter said.“After this exit, Mr Walter intends to make future sports-related investments. “Walter did not initiate the proposed transaction to sell his interest, which has been in the works for quite some time.”As 61.5% shareholders, Clearlake already had day-to-day operational control at Chelsea managed by Eghbali, and were due to make their own appointment as chairman to replace Boehly next year, but taking complete control will ease internal tensions at the club and should smooth decision making.The most immediate impact of the impending ownership change is likely to be felt in Chelsea’s plans for a new stadium, as Eghbali has clashed with Boehly over whether the club should seek to redevelop Stamford Bridge or seek an alternative site elsewhere.Walter is being investigated by the US Department of Justice over $21bn in loans which it has been alleged were not disclosed to state insurance regulators, and led to the sudden sale of assets to pay down some of the loans.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe American insurance and sports investor last month sold his 85% stake in the Los Angeles Lakers to Josh ⁠Kushner and Bob Iger in a deal that valued the NBA franchise at around £9bn.Walter’s holding company, TWG Global, subsequently issued a statement saying that the company “is not looking to sell its sports assets at ‘fire sale’ prices”.Representatives for Boehly and Clearlake declined to comment.Explore more on these topicsChelseaBusinessnewsShareReuse this content

title: Champions League: Bayern break down Bodø/Glimt, Como put four past Leipzig | Champions League | The Guardian
description: Bayern Munich were frustrated before half-time but cruised to a 5-0 victory, while the Italian newcomers made an impressive debut
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Bayern Munich were frustrated before half-time but cruised to a 5-0 victory, while the Italian newcomers made an impressive debut
Content: Michael Olise celebrates scoring the fifth of Bayern’s goals against Bodo/Glimt at the Allianz Arena.Photograph: Anna Szilágyi/EPAView image in fullscreenMichael Olise celebrates scoring the fifth of Bayern’s goals against Bodo/Glimt at the Allianz Arena.Photograph: Anna Szilágyi/EPAChampions LeagueChampions League: Bayern break down Bodø/Glimt, Como put four past LeipzigBayern Munich 5-0 Bodø/Glimt, Como 4-1 LeipzigLens win 3-2 at Slavia Prague with last-gasp doubleAgenciesThu 10 Sep 2026 17.57 EDTLast modified on Thu 10 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBayernMunichopened theirChampions Leaguecampaign with a 5-0 thrashing of Norway’sBodo/Glimt.The six-times winners were frustrated before half-time by Bodo/Glimt but cruised once Jamal Musiala smashed in the opener two minutes into the second period and the floodgates opened.Fenerbahce coach resigns after draw with Roma – but president insists he will stayRead moreHarry Kane headed the second on the hour – his 34th goal in 39 Champions League appearances for Bayern – and Alphonso Davies made it 3-0 with a powerful half-volley. With Vincent Kompany’s side in full flow, Michael ‌Olise completed the scoring with a superb late brace.Cesc Fàbregas’sComoimpressed on their debut in Europe’s premier club competition, crushingRB Lepzig4-1.Goals from Croatia midfielder Martin Baturina, Greece forward Tasos Douvikas and Senegal’s Assane Diao put Como in control. Serbia midfielder Andrija Maksimović pulled a goal back for Leipzig, before Maximo Perrone sealed a 4-1 victory late on in a dream night in northern Italy.View image in fullscreenComo manager Cesc Fàbregas gives a post-game, on-pitch team talk to his players after opening the Italian side’s Champions League campaign with a win.Photograph: Alex Pantling/UEFA/Getty ImagesTen-manSlavia Praguesuffered ​heartbreak at home toLens‌as they conceded twice in ​stoppage time to lose 3-2.Mikulas ​Konecny was sent off for the hosts just after half-time after a tackle was reviewed by VAR, but minutes later Danijel Sturm put the hosts ahead. Abdallah Sima broke Slavia’s resistance with an equaliser only for Sturm to send the home crowd into raptures with his second in the 88th minute.Florian Thauvin struck in the 91st minute and there was still time for Lens to snatch victory with a pinpoint strike by Ruben Aguilar.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionPSVcame from a goal down to draw 1-1 at home toShakhtar Donetskand end a woeful record in their opening matches of Champions League campaigns. The Dutch club had lost their opening fixtures in their last five Champions League appearances and trailed at half-time before Sergiño Dest ensured a point.Right near the end of a cagey first half, Shakhtar stunned the hosts when Gleiker Mendoza cut in from wide and ‌sent a stunning low ‌shot beyond the dive of Matej Kovar. PSV responded immediately after the break as the ‌ball was fed across the area to Dest who calmly found the bottom corner with an inch-perfect shot.Romadrew 1-1 withFenerbahcein Istanbul, with Bryan Cristante’s opener for the visitors cancelled out by Archie Brown’s goal three minutes into the second half. Confusion reigned after the match as the Fenerbahce head coach, Ismail Kartal,announced his resignation– only for the club president to insist he will stay.Explore more on these topicsChampions LeagueBayern MunichBodø/GlimtComoRB LeipzigPSV EindhovenSlavia PraguenewsShareReuse this content

title: French FA accuses Infantino of ‘seriously damaging’ football as it withdraws support | Gianni Infantino | The Guardian
description: The French Football Federation’s president, Philippe Diallo, has strongly criticised his Fifa counterpart, saying ‘trust has been broken’
Author: Raphaël Jucobin
Headline: The French Football Federation’s president, Philippe Diallo, has strongly criticised his Fifa counterpart, saying ‘trust has been broken’
Content: Gianni Infantino was accused by the French federation’s president of behaving in a ‘unilateral and opaque fashion’.Photograph: Kacper Pempel/ReutersView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino was accused by the French federation’s president of behaving in a ‘unilateral and opaque fashion’.Photograph: Kacper Pempel/ReutersGianni InfantinoFrench FA accuses Infantino of ‘seriously damaging’ football as it withdraws support‘Image and unity’ of game affected, FFF president saysIt will consult sacked former Fifa official Kevin LamourRaphaël Jucobinin ParisThu 10 Sep 2026 13.03 EDTLast modified on Thu 10 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe French Football Federation’s president, Philippe Diallo, saidGianni Infantinohad “seriously damaged the image and the unity of football” as he announced the end of France’s support for the Fifa president’s re-election.The FFF’s executive committee unanimously voted on Thursday to withdraw its backing, which had been formalised at the end of June. Diallo referred to “events during the World Cup” which had “flagrantly gone against the way we believe our sport should be run” and to Infantino’sWorld Cup sell-off plan,which was revealed in July andscrappedafter a widespread backlash.Infantino installs loyalist to oversee Caribbean as he splits Fifa managementRead moreDuring the World Cup the suspension of the US forward Folarin Balogun wasoverturnedby Fifa after lobbying from Donald Trump. The US presidentsaid he called Infantinoto recommend that Balogun be allowed to play. Fifa has said the decision taken by its disciplinary committee was“a balanced measure”and “based on an explicit provision of the applicable regulations”.Diallo outlined the reasons for the loss in confidence: “From July onwards, the conditions which led to us to support his candidacy had been disrupted. Does the withdrawal of the [sell-off] project solve the issue? I don’t think so. His initiatives during and after theWorld Cuphave seriously damaged the image and the unity of football. As a result, we believe that trust has been broken.”Diallo said of the initial decision to support Infantino: “It would be wrong to say that certain developments in football were not made under his mandate.” But he added: “When you are making changes to the game itself, in a unilateral and opaque fashion to sell our shared asset, that changes our appreciation.“France is one of the founding members ofFifa, and as such we have a historical legitimacy to intervene when we feel that Fifa and its president are deviating from our vision of how world football should be run. We also have sporting legitimacy, as one of the top three teams in the world rankings over the last 10 years. We wanted to make it clear that we refuse to go in a direction which does not correspond to the general interest of our sport.”When reports of the sell-off project came to light, the FFF expressed “doubts and deep concerns”. Uefa threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions andseveral European countries, including Wales and England, withdrew their support for Infantino but the FFF had not until Thursday publicly disavowed him.Diallo indicated France would play an active part in Uefa’s search for an alternative candidate for the Fifa presidency before the 18 November deadline. The election will take place in March during Fifa’s next congress.Before then, Diallo said, the FFF would reach out to figures it considers experts in “transparency and good governance” in football and beyond as part of France’s “contribution to the debate”, as it pushes for “far-reaching reform” of Fifa.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionHe cited Kevin Lamour, the former Fifa chief operating officer whowas dismissedafter criticising the sell-off plan, as one of the people the FFF would look to consult.Fifa was approached for comment.Explore more on these topicsGianni InfantinoFifaFootball politicsWorld CupWorld Cup 2026Sport politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Fenerbahce coach resigns after draw with Roma – but president insists he will stay | Fenerbahce | The Guardian
description: Ismail Kartal told reporters after the Champions League draw with Roma that he was leaving ‘never to return’ – but his employer had a different view
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Ismail Kartal told reporters after the Champions League draw with Roma that he was leaving ‘never to return’ – but his employer had a different view
Content: Fenerbahce have said Ismail Kartal was upset at being struck by a bottle, leading to his unexpected outburst.Photograph: Anadolu/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenFenerbahce have said Ismail Kartal was upset at being struck by a bottle, leading to his unexpected outburst.Photograph: Anadolu/Getty ImagesFenerbahceFenerbahce coach resigns after draw with Roma – but president insists he will stayIsmail Kartal tells reporters he will leave ‘never to return’Club president: ‘I am his senior, I told him to continue’Reuters andGuardian sportThu 10 Sep 2026 18.20 EDTLast modified on Thu 10 Sep 2026 18.50 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Fenerbahce head coach, Ismail Kartal, announced his resignation on Thursday after ⁠his team drew 1-1 at home to Roma in theChampions League– but minutes ⁠later, the club ⁠president ​said Kartal would stay in the job.Kartal shocked the post-match press conference by claiming he was ⁠leavingFenerbahce“never to return”. The 65-year-old added that he was taking the drastic decision “to clear the way for the club” – but the Fenerbahce president, Aziz Yildrim, quickly moved to play down his manager’s remarks.Champions League: Bayern break down Bodø/Glimt, Como put four past LeipzigRead moreMinutes after ⁠the press conference, Yildirim told reporters that ​Kartal “continues in his role” with the Turkish side. “Some ‌fans threw a bottle ‌at the coach’s head this evening during the game.
